headline: Security Agencies Stall Traffic for Three Hours While Debating Whose Turn It Is to Open a Single Gate
body:
Q: We are reporting live from the barricades where two security agencies have been in a deadlock since 9:00 AM. Mr. Sharma, as a senior security consultant, can you explain the holdup?

A: It is a simple matter of jurisdictional etiquette. The agency protecting the politician believes that opening the gate falls under 'logistical crowd control,' while the paramilitary unit argues that touching the gate handle constitutes a 'threat-assessment maneuver' that they are specifically trained to perform.

Q: So, the gate remains closed because they can’t agree on who holds the title of 'Gatekeeper'?

A: Exactly. One side has threatened to file a formal complaint with the Home Ministry if the other reaches for the latch. Meanwhile, the politician is currently inside his SUV playing Candy Crush, and we have a traffic jam that now stretches all the way to the neighboring district.

Q: Is there any end in sight to this standoff?

A: We are expecting a compromise by evening. They are currently drafting a Memorandum of Understanding that will allow both agencies to place their hands on the gate simultaneously, ensuring that no single entity takes unilateral credit for entry.
caption: When the ego gets in the way of the exit, nobody goes home. A standoff at the city gate proves that security is less about protection and more about professional posturing. #SecurityDrama #TrafficJam #ProtocolWars #DelhiLife (satire)
igHook: Tag someone who would rather argue for three hours than just open the door.
